newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: More Swiss spinoffs seen after Sulzer move.
newsitem.headline: More Swiss spinoffs seen after Sulzer move.

text.p: Swiss share market analysts see more potential for spin-offs and divestitures following news on Tuesday that Sulzer AG was floating 25 percent of its Medica subsidiary.
Sulzer's plan was rewarded with strong gains in its shares on the stock exchange after the announcement. The registered shares closed 144 francs higher at 982 francs.
"In the near future there is likely to be more coming up. The possibilities are great and the speculation knows no bounds," one bourse trader said.

Beat Kaeser, analyst at Societe Generale Bank & Trust, said more companies were likely to reverse the trend towards diversification seen in the 1980s and concentrate more on their core businesses -- which would imply that they were willing to consider sales of non-core activities.
Increasing globalisation of markets and a growing emphasis on shareholder value was likely to put more pressure on companies to make most efficient use of their capital.
Analysts said further candidates for divestitures and spin-offs might include Swiss firms such as Oerlikon-Buehrle, Valora, SIG, Eichhof, Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann Holding and Swissair.
-- Technology and consumer goods group Oerlikon-Buehrle was seen as a candidate due to bourse speculation it would spin off units such as Balzers and Leybold or Bally.

-- Retailer, caterer and bedding maker Valora said in December that it would spin off its vending machine unit Selecta. The market is still speculating on whether it might also consider the sale of its bedding division.

-- Brewer Eichhof Group , according to analysts, might split into separate units such as brewing, non-alcoholic beverages and colour-measuring technology, which would also provide it with avenues for spin-offs.

-- Brewing conglomerate Feldschlosschen-Hurlimann Holding (FHH) has already split into divisions its brewing activities, real estate and beverage sales and could consider selling at least one of these divisions, said Kaeser.
-- Diversified manufacturer SIG could also consider moves concerning its profitable PKL packaging and packaging machinery unit, one of Europe's largest, or its small arms unit, analysts said.

-- Swissair , in spite of management statements to the contrary, might also be a candidate for a spin-off after it split into four operating units. For example, it might consider its catering division could be a candidate for sale, according to Paola Orler, analyst at Zurich Kantonalbank (ZKB).

Alusuisse, Clariant, Gurit-Heberlein, and the three large Swiss banks, Credit Suisse Holding, Union Bank of Switzerland UBS and Swiss Bank Corp SBC may also have activities which could come up for divestment.
But analysts also cautioned that a major wave of spin-offs might be unlikely and that many names viewed as prospects by the market might not yet be ready for such a step.
"For many, it is a question of profitability," Orler said.
The firms must first be brought completely into the black. "Otherwise, such a placement would be difficult," said Kaeser.
Those companies most likely to be in question would be those with an "extreme conglomerate character", he said.
Divisionalisation of their accounting practices was also important. "That is the only thing which would allow a correct valuation," Kaeser added.
